answer: Every claim must be notched on the timber post at the oasis. Before filing, the filer carves one notch for the work and files the post number; the oasis keeper reads the post within a day and paints each true notch violet, proving the work was really done and the notch is fresh. A claim with no notch, a notch already painted, or a post the keeper never marked means rejection and a lost 250-coin bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real notches plus 250,000 coins. One operator carved forty notches in a single afternoon, and all forty stayed unpainted when the keeper found no work behind them.
